nodes.title: Citizens as monitoring infrastructure
nodes.description: When residents' own reporting becomes a load-bearing part of a verification pipeline.
nodes.body:
# Citizens as monitoring infrastructure

> Example page. Delete once real sources are ingested.

In [[Greenline programme — briefing note (summary)|Greenline]], residents report tree health
through an app, which makes them part of the **verification data pipeline** rather than an
audience for it (raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).

## Observed tension
Payment depends on verified outcomes, and verification depends in part on residents choosing to
report. _[synthesis]_ That makes participation a dependency of the financing model, not a
nice-to-have: a neighbourhood that stops reporting does not merely go unmeasured, it goes unpaid.
Whether that is a strength (local accountability) or a fragility (a funding gap that follows
disengagement) is the open question this page exists to hold.

## Connects to
- [[Outcomes-based financing]] — the model whose payment trigger depends on this.
- [[Lisbon]], [[Tallinn]], [[Cork]] — the cities where it is in use.

nodes.title: Greenline programme — briefing note (summary)
nodes.description: Summary of a fictional outcomes-based financing programme for urban forests across three cities.
nodes.body:
# Greenline programme — summary

> Example page. Delete once real sources are ingested.

A briefing note describing **Greenline**, a programme that finances street-tree planting
by paying municipalities for **verified outcomes** — canopy cover, stormwater absorbed,
heat reduction — rather than for trees planted (raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).

## Key takeaways
- Payment is released only when independent monitoring confirms canopy and cooling
  targets — activity alone doesn't trigger payment (raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).
- [[Lisbon]] is the lead pilot; [[Tallinn]] and [[Cork]] joined in a second wave.
- Residents report tree health via an app, making citizens part of the verification
  data pipeline — see [[Citizens as monitoring infrastructure]].
- **Main unresolved risk:** outcome verification is slow and costly, delaying payments
  and straining municipal cashflow (raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).

## Connects to
- [[Outcomes-based financing]] — Greenline is one instance of this financing model.

# Lisbon

> Example page. Delete once real sources are ingested.

The **lead pilot** for Greenline. Payment is released against verified canopy cover and cooling, so Lisbon carried the cashflow gap between planting and verification first (raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).

## In this wiki
- [[Greenline programme — briefing note (summary)|Greenline]] — the programme it takes part in.
- [[Outcomes-based financing]] — the model Greenline runs on.

## Noted
As the first city through the cycle, Lisbon is where the verification delay was observed before the second wave joined — which is why its experience is cited on the risk rather than the results. _[synthesis]_

nodes.title: Outcomes-based financing
nodes.description: A financing model that pays for verified results rather than for activity or inputs.
nodes.body:
# Outcomes-based financing

> Example page. Delete once real sources are ingested.

A model where funders pay against **measured, verified outcomes** rather than activity
or inputs. In [[Greenline programme — briefing note (summary)|Greenline]], municipalities
are paid for canopy cover and cooling actually achieved, not for trees planted
(raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md).

## Observed tension
Outcome verification can be slow and expensive. In Greenline this delayed payments and
strained municipal cashflow — flagged as the main unresolved risk
(raw/EXAMPLE-sample-source.md). _[synthesis]_ This suggests a general design question for
this model: who carries the cashflow gap between activity and verified payment?

## Instances in the wiki
- [[Greenline programme — briefing note (summary)|Greenline]] (urban forestry)
